title: Alfonso II d'Este to the protonotary at Venice, 14 Apr 1576, cc. 76-77 (catalogue 1566): key recovered from the ciphertext, letter read, by a narrow margin

steps.what: Fetched the leaves by IIIF. No decipherment on them.
Pass 1 on straightened half-lines, written down before any value was known. One change, z to 7 at c. 76r l. 2, was made without a log entry and has been logged since.
Quadgram search on period Italian, 10 restarts, no crib. Eight of ten runs landed on one solution, which read as Italian apart from the nulls.

c. 76r and the rest broken separately. Not set up in advance: the whole-text key is 21 minutes older than the split, and whoever ran it knew the key. Key from c. 76r on the rest scores -10.17 per position; 200 shuffled tables, best -13.38. Reproduced with a separate model: -10.18; 500 shuffled tables, best -13.56.
Pass 2, not blind: the reading walked against the signs, 50 disagreements viewed on crops, 14 signs changed.

Independent AI check of the first version, sign-first on 287 signs: 6 raw disagreements (2.1%), transcription wrong at 2 (0.7%). A sealed tail test, 37 of 37 plus 17 of 17, refuted the first version's claim that one shape stood for g and q. Its other findings are in VERIFY.md.
Pass 3: q and g split, all 339 read by tail; 338 agree with sense, 1 conflict at c. 77r l. 9. Not language-blind. c. 76r l. 2 corrected. Marks rebuilt and enforced by check_marks.py.
Recount: 740 words, 737 as sense, 706 with no restored or changed letter (95.4%). Bar 703.
Web searches only; the Modena State Archive series were not opened.

outcome.method_basis: Quadgram search on the signs with no crib, tested by breaking c. 76r and the rest separately. That hold-out was not set up in advance.
outcome.fraction_read_source: scripts/check_marks.py 76: 706 of 740 words carry no restored, changed or doubtful letter; 737 of 740 read as sense. By hand: first 535 of 557 (96.1%), second and postscript 171 of 183 (93.4%). The margin over the bar is three words.

texts.label: Alfonso II d'Este to the protonotary, 14 Apr 1576, cc. 76-77

reading_review.by: AI language-model agent (for WAINUT; a model reading, not a person), independent of the solver
reading_review.note: Read as sentences 3 Nov 2026. I read the Italian sentence by sentence against the decryption file and the English: all 15 numbered sentences make coherent, idiomatic 16th-century chancery Italian with a consistent argument (the unnamed man, the health deputies, the extradition agreement with Venice, fifty scudi via Tassone; then oils and almonds, a Roman complaint, the Rovigo prisoners), and the English follows the Italian closely. The holes are scattered rather than in every sentence: doubtful [?puntino], 'a [?ti]' (the Pope's title is missing) and [?gagliarde]; about 30 restored letters, mostly the eight l-for-r slips plus blots; and 'mostrare' in sentence 12 is restored against a clear tail that gives 'sotrare'. The second hand is left in raw single-consonant spelling ('fato', 'efeto', 'posiamo'), which is readable. Minor points: 'che lla lo farebbe' is better read as 'là' (there, i.e. Venice) than 'she'; the signature and the docket are not resolved; and the 95.4% figure clears the bar by only three words.

texts.summary: The duke tells his agent how to handle an unnamed man who fears stricter proceedings: he was never in Este pay, Ferrara cannot shelter him, and he is to get fifty scudi. A second hand turns to oils and almonds, a Roman complaint and the prisoners of Rovigo.
texts.note: Words 740: as sense 737, no restored or changed letter 706. English stands in the reading file, sentence by sentence.

outcome.notes: Open checks, not unread pieces of the cipher, are in NOTES.md: second-hand strokes above signs not recorded, no fresh key-free copy of the whole text, clear end and signature a first reading.

validation.notes: The key was tested in the target's own split, which was not set up in advance: -10.17 against best -13.38 of 200 shuffled tables, reproduced at -10.18 against best -13.56 of 500. docs/_validate.py was not run.

prior.where: Web searches on 2-3 Nov 2026 found no edition or decipherment. The docket of c. 77v shows that the letter was read in its own day. Not opened: ASMo, Cancelleria ducale, Cifrario (8 buste) and the ambassadors' series. Search results do not settle this.

human: WAINUT set the task (catalogue 1566) and the rules; AI language-model agents transcribed, built the key, read and checked. No target-specific human intervention. No human palaeographer checked the text.
